title: Update SDK examples + config snippets for batching tiers (Python/TS/Go)
creator: Alex Martinez
description:
Goal
- Update customer-facing SDK examples and config snippets to demonstrate:
  1) selecting a batching tier: fast | standard | cost_efficient
  2) overriding specific batching knobs safely (e.g., max_queue_delay_ms) while keeping tier defaults for everything else
  3) how to confirm the effective config (Console + explain endpoint / response headers when available)

Why
- Tiered batching defaults are intended to be the safe on-ramp. Customers are asking (Support + SE) how tiers interact with explicit overrides and how to validate what they’re actually running.
- We need consistent terminology across docs + SDKs (cost_efficient, not eco) and examples that do not imply breaking API changes.

Scope
- Python SDK: update README snippets + examples folder (chat/completions + embeddings) to include batching_tier.
- TypeScript SDK: update examples + typing (if required) + docsstrings.
- Go SDK: update examples to include batching_tier; ensure request serialization is correct.
- Provide 2 patterns per language:
  - pattern A: “just pick a tier”
  - pattern B: “pick a tier + override one knob (queue delay) for streaming vs non-streaming”
- Add a short FAQ-style note in examples README: precedence rules (explicit override wins), plus warnings about streaming cadence.

Non-goals
- Adding new public API surface beyond the batching_tier parameter already planned.
- Full docs-site information architecture (tracked in batching-profiles-docs-plan / DevEx docs ticket).

References
- PRD: Confluence /product-docs/requirements/workload-aware-batching-defaults-prd
- Design spec: Confluence /product-docs/design-specs/workload-aware-batching-defaults-design-spec
- Precedence thread: Slack eng-runtime thread-1740849901
- Effective config explain endpoint: redwood PR-18470 (in flight)

Open questions
- Confirm final user-facing enum string: cost_efficient vs cost-efficient (code uses cost_efficient today; docs should match code).
- Do we want to show both “tier only” and “tier + overrides” in the quickstart, or keep quickstart minimal and push overrides to an advanced page?

Acceptance criteria
- Each SDK repo has at least 2 updated examples (chat/completions + embeddings or rerank) showing batching_tier usage.
- Each language includes one example demonstrating an override (max_queue_delay_ms and/or max_batch_size) with a note that explicit overrides take precedence.
- Examples compile/run in CI (or existing example test harness) and do not change any existing method signatures (no breaking changes).
- Terminology is consistent across languages and matches runtime config schema.
- Examples include a short validation note: “check Console Effective Config” and/or “use /v1/config/explain when available” (behind flag) with graceful language if not enabled.

Proposed example content (draft)

Python (chat, tier only)
- client.responses.create(..., batching_tier="standard")

Python (streaming, tier + override)
- client.responses.create(..., stream=True, batching_tier="fast", batching={"max_queue_delay_ms": 2})
- Note: streaming workloads are sensitive to queue delay; if cadence degrades, prefer fast tier and keep max_queue_delay_ms low.

TypeScript (tier only)
- await client.responses.create({ model, input, batching_tier: "standard" })

TypeScript (tier + override)
- await client.responses.create({ model, input, batching_tier: "cost_efficient", batching: { max_queue_delay_ms: 12 } })
- Note: cost_efficient may increase tail latency at high concurrency; watch p95 and timeout rate.

Go (tier only)
- req := redwood.ResponsesCreateRequest{ Model: model, Input: input, BatchingTier: redwood.String("standard") }

Go (tier + override)
- req := ... BatchingTier: "standard", Batching: &redwood.BatchingConfig{ MaxQueueDelayMS: redwood.Int(6) }

(Exact request structs/fields may differ; adapt to each SDK’s naming conventions.)
implementation_notes:
Implementation approach
- Keep examples conservative and aligned with SRE guidance:
  - fast: prioritize latency/cadence, minimal queueing
  - standard: balanced defaults, recommended default for most customers
  - cost_efficient: more batching/queueing allowed, must mention overload protection + higher tail risk

Precedence rule callout (must be consistent across examples)
- If batching_tier is set and batching.* overrides are set, the overrides win for those fields, and the tier fills in everything else.
- If customer already set explicit batching config historically, adding batching_tier should not silently change behavior (explicit config continues to take precedence).

Validation / observability callout
- Where possible, show how to confirm effective config:
  - Console: “Effective config” panel (ENG-18425)
  - API: /v1/config/explain (PR-18470) or response headers when available
  - Metrics: queue_delay_ms histogram, batch_size histogram (ENG-18422)

Risks
- Don’t over-promise exact latency numbers in examples.
- Don’t suggest overriding too many knobs; keep it to one knob to demonstrate precedence and caution.

Test plan
- Add/extend example tests that assert request payload serialization includes batching_tier and batching overrides.
- Smoke test locally against staging for one model in beta cohort once flag enabled (coordinate with Release Eng thread).
